game.summary: Restored rubbings-theft-001's snapshot (a9b0961) except features/; `git diff --stat` against it was empty before any edit, and every path it touched is owned. Finding 1: each player's status now carries settledChoice and choiceDeadline (schema, MatchRoom notices, MatchView, HeadlessClient). A new purse-choice line says 'You chose X' / 'They chose X' / 'Taken by default: X', with the server's settled-at and deadline ticks as data attributes. Key and click handling is extracted into the pure chosenTheftType (hud.ts), and main.ts uses it. Web unit tests cover choiceLine plus key 1, key 2, clicks on options 1 and 2, and inputs that pick nothing. A new integration test runs through the real room: the guest holds both types, the host neither, and the host sends choose-theft for the type defaultTheftType would not take; the test checks settlement.choice === 'winner' and that the type moved. The default-deadline test now also asserts settledChoice 'default'. theft-loop now clicks '1: Moon' and asserts the host sees 'You chose Moon' (never 'Taken by default'), the guest sees 'They chose Moon', and deadline - settledAt >= 60 server ticks on both pages. I also added an untagged Playwright test that clicks the second of two options (the non-default Moon). Finding 2: a new expectRoomChecks helper (tracker uses it too) runs after every test in match, visibility and admission. 'removes a ship when its player leaves' also asserts the ledger player is 'left' and the room checks are clean. This surfaced a real bug: a join refused in onJoin still reached onDrop/onLeave and made the ledger refuse disconnectPlayer and quitPlayer for an unknown player. Both hooks now skip sessions the room never admitted. Finding 3: MatchTuning.random is a test-only seam (default cryptoRandom = node:crypto randomInt) and now supplies the world, ledger and duel seeds. New tests/integration/ledgerSeed.test.ts (source layout off) checks two seeds deal differently via createMatchLedger, then shows two matches with different codes and the same source get the same deal, and another source changes the deal. New apps/server/src/random.test.ts mocks node:crypto and shows the default source calls randomInt(0, 2**32) with sourceLayout off. Docs: architecture.md and README. Checks run from a fresh npm ci: typecheck ok; unit 905/905; integration 75/75 in 127 s (vitest 126 s; the sequential harness group is ~65 s of it); build ok. Browser: 9/9 passed (8 scenarios + 1 untagged) in 251 s, and check-report passed on that JSON report.
open_assumptions: PROTOCOL_VERSION is not bumped again for the two new PlayerStatus fields (settledChoice, choiceDeadline). The snapshot already bumped it to 6 for this unreleased feature, and no released client decodes these fields.
The loser's notice reads 'They chose Moon' (the winner's own reads 'You chose Moon'). The task fixed only the winner's wording and the default's.
The choice notice is a separate purse line (data-testid purse-choice) under the existing settlement line, so the existing settlement texts and their tests stay unchanged.

So room.invariantViolations and room.ledgerRefusals are never asserted for that match. The server keeps checkInvariants on, so a violation would only reach console.error and the test would still pass. # Decisions: rubbings-theft-fixes

From the overnight session of 2026-09-25. The operator is asleep and asked the assistant to decide, record each decision, and use the workflow for the code.

## Decisions

- rubbings-theft-001 passed every check (8/8 browser). Its coverage reviewer blocked it on an untested theft-choice UI, and the general reviewer was stopped before a verdict. This follow-up restores its snapshot (`a9b0961`) on its base (`54f7e72`), so the whole feature is reviewed again.
- The settlement notice says whether the winner chose ("You chose …") or the default applied ("Taken by default: …"), which also helps players understand what happened. Corrected after design challenge attempt 1: `theft-loop` keeps its pinned shape (one option, clicked, with the notice proving it came from the click, well before the deadline in server ticks). The two-option, non-default choice is proven in an integration test through the room and in web unit tests.
- The ledger seed's privacy is shown through an injected randomness seam, and the production source is `node:crypto`.
- The `theft-loop` policy wording now says "tapping attack keys" (duel buttons fire on the press).

## Assumptions

- Everything in `features/rubbings-theft/` stands.

## Deferred

- `match-online` (the lobby, timer, claim, final island, results) comes next.

concerns.message: theft-loop's '≥60 ticks before choiceDeadline' assertion assumes the e2e server keeps the full 100-tick (5 s) theft window, which leaves 40 world ticks (2 s) from the window opening to the click. The integration suite already uses test-only rule overrides through createLedger({ rules }). If the e2e server path shares those overrides or shortened encounter timings, the window may be under 60 ticks and the assertion can never pass. The 2 s budget also assumes the snapshot's client shows the choice options as soon as the options message arrives. If they wait behind a K.O./result banner or the arena-to-sea transition, the budget is tighter than it looks. Separately, 'server ticks' must mean the ledger's 20 Hz world ticks. The room also has a 60 Hz match clock, and 60 ticks of that clock is 1 s, not 3 s.
concerns.consequence: If any of these assumptions fails, theft-loop either fails every run or fails intermittently on this shared, loaded machine. The browser check then costs a verification attempt (3 max), or the worker weakens the margin to get it green.

concerns.message: In the integration test, the winner must send the type `defaultTheftType` would NOT pick. After the guest collects one of each type, the free-source counts are tied (3 and 3), so the default falls back to the fixed type order. If the test hard-codes 'the second type', a later change to the layout or to who collects what can make the chosen type equal the default. It should compute the default from the room's ledger state (defaultTheftType and eligibleTheftTypes are exported from the objectives index) and assert that the sent type differs from it, as well as asserting settlement.choice === 'winner'.
concerns.consequence: With a hard-coded type, the test can silently stop proving a non-default choice. The coverage reviewer blocks again on the same finding.

concerns.message: Finding 2's invariant assertions can pass without checking anything. The per-tick check runs inside advance(). If a test tears down the room right after the leave, and the quit is handled in onLeave, no tick runs between the ship's removal and the assertion, so `invariantViolations` is empty by default. This matters most in match.test.ts's 'removes a ship when its player leaves' and in admission tests where joins are refused.
concerns.consequence: Vacuous assertions let a regression in the quit path (a ship removed while the ledger still counts its player) through, and the coverage reviewer can flag the finding as not really fixed. The tracker should also assert that it saw at least one tick after the leave.

concerns.message: The seed-privacy test must show that the deal follows the injected source and not the match code. If the worker sends all of the room's randomness through the new seam, including match-code generation, then 'same source → same deal' also gives the same code, and the test can't tell the two apart. Also, assignSources reduces the seed to 32 bits (`seed >>> 0`), so different injected values can collapse to the same seed. The test has to check that its two seeds give different deals after that reduction, which the plan already asks for. Finally, spying on node:crypto's randomInt only works with vi.mock hoisting. vi.spyOn on an ESM namespace fails.
concerns.consequence: The test can pass while the deal still depends on the match code, or the spy approach can fail at typecheck or at runtime and cost rework.

concerns.message: The new integration tests add room time: the guest collects both types (two 6 s channels unless the rules are overridden), and the seed test builds at least three rooms. The snapshot's integration duration isn't recorded here, and the acceptance says the suite must stay 'well inside' its budget.
concerns.consequence: Without the collection-time overrides the suite may drift toward the 300 s check timeout. The worker then has to retrofit overrides or parallelism late in the run.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Keep the plan, with two changes. In theft-loop, treat settlement.choice === 'winner' (shown as the host's 'You chose …' notice) as the proof that the click happened before the deadline, because only chooseTheft can produce that value. Measure the margin as settlement.tick minus the tick the window opened, and require it to be at most 40 ticks, which is the same as being at least 60 ticks before the deadline. Read it from room diagnostics, and don't add protocol fields just for the test. For the seed, inject a plain `() => number` seed source into the room, used only for the ledger. The room test calls assignSources with the chosen seeds to confirm the deals differ, then checks that the room's sources match assignSources(sites, source()) whatever the match code.
challenge.cheap_experiment: Right after restoring the snapshot, before other changes: (1) grep the e2e server entry and test settings for theftChoiceTicks and other rule overrides, to confirm the browser server keeps the 100-tick window; (2) add a temporary click on the single option to theft-loop and log the window-open tick, settlement.tick and choiceDeadline from room diagnostics over 5 runs on this machine. If the worst-case margin is well above 60 ticks, keep the plan. If not, move the choice UI in front of the result banner or transition first.

# Task: game

## Goal

Deliver `rubbings-theft` (collect → fight → steal → recover through the ledger) with its review findings fixed. Run rubbings-theft-001 built it and passed every check, including all eight browser scenarios. Its coverage reviewer blocked it because the theft-choice UI isn't really tested, and its general reviewer was stopped before a verdict. Start from that run's snapshot, fix the findings, and the whole feature is reviewed again.

## Context

- `features/rubbings-theft/game-task.md` and `decisions.md` define the feature, and all of it still applies. Read them first.
- **First step:** restore rubbings-theft-001's snapshot (commit `a9b0961`) into your worktree, deletions included, but not `features/`:
  `git restore --source=refs/workflow/d03bbf0cf3c28b7b/game --staged --worktree -- . ':!features'`.
  Check with `git diff --stat refs/workflow/d03bbf0cf3c28b7b/game -- . ':!features'` (it must print nothing). Then read `docs/architecture.md`, `apps/web/src/main.ts` (the theft-choice handlers near lines 186–203), `apps/web/src/rubbings.ts`, `tests/e2e/theftLoop.spec.ts`, `tests/integration/seaDuelSetup.ts` (`tracker()`) and `apps/server/src/objectives.ts`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Findings to fix (coverage reviewer)

1. **(P1) The theft-choice UI is proven** (settled after design challenge attempt 1).
   - **The notice says who chose:** "You chose Moon" or "Taken by default: Moon", from the ledger's `settlement.choice`. The loser's notice says which too.
   - **`theft-loop` keeps exactly its pinned description.** The host collects one type and the guest the other, so the winner's choice has one option. The winner **clicks** that option. The test asserts:
     - the host's notice says "You chose …", not "Taken by default";
     - the guest's notice names the choice;
     - the settlement happened at least **60 server ticks** (3 s) before `choiceDeadline`. Read both from the room's diagnostics or the settlement message, not the browser's clock.
   - **The two-option, non-default choice is proven below the browser:**
     - an integration test through the real room: the guest holds both types and the winner neither; the winner sends `choose-theft` for the type `defaultTheftType` would **not** pick; `settlement.choice === "winner"` and that type moved;
     - the key and click handling is extracted into a small pure function (key 1 or 2, or a click on option n, gives the chosen type), with web unit tests for key 1, key 2 and clicks on both options; `main.ts` is wired to it;
     - optionally, a second Playwright test **without a scenario tag** clicks the second of two options in the browser.
2. **(P2) The per-tick invariant everywhere.** `tests/integration/match.test.ts`, `visibility.test.ts` and `admission.test.ts` also run through `MatchRoom`. Assert `room.invariantViolations` is empty (through `tracker()` or an equivalent) in each, including `match.test.ts`'s "removes a ship when its player leaves", which now goes through the quit path.
3. **(P2) The ledger's seed is private.**
   - Inject the room's randomness source through a test-only seam.
   - A room-level test shows the ledger deal follows that source, not the match code: two matches with the same source give the same deal. For two sources, choose seed values the test first verifies give different deals (8 sites over 2 types have only 70 layouts), then show that the deal changes with the source for the same code.
   - The production default is `node:crypto`'s `randomInt`: a unit test of the default source shows it is called. The test-only source-layout setting must be off in these tests.

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Apart from restoring the snapshot, change only what the findings need. Keep the structure, names, every scenario id and every existing test.
- Tests drive input like players do.

## Acceptance

- The restored `rubbings-theft` feature meets all of `features/rubbings-theft/game-task.md`'s acceptance.
- Findings 1–3 are fixed with the tests they name.
- `npm ci` then each of the five policy checks passes from a clean checkout, with all eight browser scenarios. The integration suite stays well inside its time budget (report the duration).

Browser checks: each scenario id appears in exactly one test title as `[scenario:<id>]`. That test, when it passes, attaches exactly one image/png named `screenshot:<id>` (other attachments are fine). The verifier refuses anything else. Before completing, run the spec files you changed with a JSON report:

```bash
WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=worker PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE=<tmp>/report.json \
  npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts --reporter=json <spec files>
```

Then check the report with the verifier's own rules: run the exact `check-report` command the controller appends to this task when it pins it.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

- Restoring the snapshot fails or touches a path outside the owned paths.
- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).
- A check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths.
- After ninety minutes of work, any required check still fails and you cannot name the next fix.

Report `question` only for a choice that would change this acceptance.

scenarios.description: One browser creates a private match from the landing page; the HUD shows the code, the protocol version, one player and a connected status.
Two browsers join the same private match with their ships in sight of each other; one sails with the keyboard and the other browser's view shows that ship at the new server-authoritative position.
A browser sails its ship around a shoal to an island dock with the keyboard and docks there; the HUD shows the dock and the ship stops at it.
Two browsers in one match with their ships out of sight of each other: neither view lists or draws the other ship until one sails within the sight radius, and it disappears again when it sails away.

One browser opens a practice duel against the dummy, lands a jab and then a keyboard throw (J then K a frame apart); the dummy's health bar and the HUD drop by the move data's damage, and hitboxes can be shown.

Two browsers: one creates a duel, the other joins by its code; after the countdown the first lands a strike on the second, and both views show the same authoritative health, round clock and result, with the connection line showing input delay and corrections.

Two browsers in one match are placed within grapple range; the host sails at the guest and presses J; both see the grapple telegraph, then a three-second countdown and the arena; the duel is decided; the winner returns to the sea with protection shown, and the loser sees a respawn countdown and then their ship at a dock.

Two browsers moored at different islands each hold E and collect a different rubbing type; the host grapples the guest at sea, wins the duel by tapping attack keys, and picks the guest's type within five seconds; the host's HUD shows both types and more gold, the guest's shows the loss.
